mcq.q: A = {1, 2, 3}, B = {4, 5} aur R = {(1, 4), (3, 5)}. Matrix mein row 3, column 5 ka element kya hoga?
mcq.explanation: (3, 5) ∈ R, so the entry is 1.

mcq.q: R = {(1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 4)} ka domain kya hai?
mcq.explanation: Domain = first elements = {1, 2, 3}.

mcq.q: Same R = {(1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 4)} ka range kya hai?
mcq.explanation: Range = second elements = {2, 4}.

mcq.q: A = {1, 2} aur B = {3, 4} ho to A × B kya hai?
mcq.explanation: A × B mein har x ∈ A ko har y ∈ B ke saath pair banate hain.

mcq.q: Agar |A| = 3 ho, to A × A mein kitne ordered pairs honge?
A = {1, 2, 3} par R = {(1, 2), (2, 3)} kaisa relation hai?
mcq.explanation: (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3) mein se koi bhi R mein nahi hai, isliye irreflexive hai.
(1, 2) ∈ R lekin (2, 1) ∉ R, isliye symmetric nahi hai.

mcq.q: R = {(x, y) | x + y, 3 se divisible hai} on A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}: kya yeh equivalence relation hai?
options: Reflexive nahi, kyunki 1 + 1 = 2 divisible by 3 nahi hai
mcq.explanation: Reflexive ke liye (1, 1) ∈ R hona chahiye, lekin 1 + 1 = 2 3 se divisible nahi hai.

mcq.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par 'a divides b' (R = {(a, b) | a | b}) kya POSET hai?
options: Haan: reflexive, anti-symmetric aur transitive hai
mcq.explanation: a | a (reflexive), a | b aur b | a ho to a = b (anti-symmetric), a | b aur b | c ho to a | c (transitive).

mcq.q: f: N → N, f(x) = x² kya function hai?
options: Haan, har x ka ek hi image hai
Nahi, kyunki x² kabhi negative ho sakta hai
Nahi, kyunki range N se alag hai
mcq.explanation: Har natural number x ka x² ek hi value deta hai aur woh N mein hai, isliye function hai.

mcq.q: f: Z → Z, f(x) = x / 2 kya function hai?
options: Nahi, f(1) = 1/2 Z mein nahi hai
mcq.explanation: f(1) = 1/2 integer nahi hai, isliye f, Z se Z mein function nahi hai.

mcq.q: f(x) = 2x aur g(x) = x + 1 ho to (f ∘ g)(3) kitna hai?
Same f(x) = 2x aur g(x) = x + 1 ke liye (g ∘ f)(3) kitna hai?
Compatibility relation kya hota hai?
mcq.explanation: Compatibility relation = reflexive + symmetric.

mcq.q: 3 elements wale set A par kitne alag relations banaye ja sakte hain?
mcq.explanation: |A × A| = 9, isliye relations = 2^9 = 512.

mcq.q: |A| = 3 aur |B| = 2 ho to A se B tak kitne alag relations possible hain?
mcq.explanation: |A × B| = 6, isliye relations = 2^6 = 64.

mcq.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(x, y) | x > y} anti-symmetric hai?
mcq.explanation: (x, y) ∈ R ke liye (y, x) ∈ R kabhi nahi hota, isliye anti-symmetric hai.

mcq.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(a, b) | a + b divisible by 3} ka sahi conclusion kya hai?
mcq.explanation: (1, 1) ∉ R (not reflexive), (3, 3) ∈ R (not irreflexive), R symmetric hai, aur (1, 2), (2, 1) dono hain (not anti-symmetric).

mcq.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} se B = {1, ..., 25} tak f(x) = x² function hai?
options: Haan, har x ka ek hi image hai
mcq.explanation: f(1) = 1, f(2) = 4, ..., f(5) = 25 — sab B mein hain aur har x ka ek image hai.

mcq.q: f: R → R, f(x) = 2x + 3 bijective function hai?
options: Haan, one-one aur onto dono hai
mcq.explanation: Linear function (slope 2 ≠ 0) R → R par one-one aur onto hai, isliye bijective hai.

mcq.q: f(x) = x + 3 ho to (f ∘ f)(x) kya hai?
f(x) = x + 3 aur g(x) = 3x − 4 ho to (g ∘ g)(x) kya hai?
A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(x, y) | x ≥ y} POSET hai?
mcq.explanation: x ≥ x (reflexive), x ≥ y aur y ≥ x sirf x = y par (anti-symmetric), aur chains transitive hain — isliye POSET hai.

mcq.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par R = {(a, b) | a + b = 2} kaisa relation hai?
mcq.explanation: R = {(1, 1)}: (1, 1) ∈ R (irreflexive nahi), (2, 2) ∉ R (reflexive nahi).

short.q: A = {a, b} aur B = {1} ho to A × B aur B × A likho.
A = {1, 2, 3} se B = {2, 3, 4, 5} tak R = {(x, y) | y = x + 1}. R likho, domain aur range nikaalo.
A = B = {1, 2, 3} par R = {(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 1)} ka matrix representation banao.
short.answer: Row 1: 0 1 0. Row 2: 0 0 1. Row 3: 1 0 0. (Rows aur columns 1, 2, 3 ke order mein.)

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par R = {(a, b) | a < b} ko listing method mein likho.

short.answer: Haan. Har a ∈ A ke liye (a, a) ∈ R hai, isliye R reflexive hai (1, 2 wala pair iske liye zaroori nahi).

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(a, b) | a + b = 6} reflexive hai, irreflexive hai ya dono nahi?
short.answer: R = {(1, 5), (2, 4), (3, 3), (4, 2), (5, 1)}. (1, 1) ∉ R, isliye reflexive nahi. (3, 3) ∈ R, isliye irreflexive nahi. Answer: dono nahi (neither).

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3} par R = {(1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 3), (3, 2)} symmetric aur anti-symmetric dono check karo.
short.answer: Symmetric: haan, har pair ka reverse R mein hai. Anti-symmetric: nahi, kyunki (1, 2) aur (2, 1) dono R mein hain aur 1 ≠ 2.

short.q: A = {1, 2} par R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2)} anti-symmetric hai ya nahi?
short.answer: Haan. Sirf (1, 2) ∈ R hai aur (2, 1) ∉ R. (1, 1) aur (2, 2) mein a = b hai, isliye anti-symmetric hai.
Nahi. (2, 1) ∈ R aur (1, 3) ∈ R, lekin (2, 3) ∉ R. Isliye transitive nahi hai.

short.q: A = {1, 2} par R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (2, 1)} transitive hai ya nahi?
short.answer: Haan. Saare chains check karo: (1, 2)(2, 1) → (1, 1) ∈ R; (2, 1)(1, 2) → (2, 2) ∈ R; baaki chains mein bhi result R mein hai.

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par R = {(a, b) | a − b, 2 se divisible hai} equivalence relation hai? Reason do.
short.answer: Haan. Reflexive: a − a = 0. Symmetric: a − b even ho to b − a bhi even. Transitive: a − b aur b − c even ho to a − c bhi even. Classes: {1, 3} aur {2, 4}.
Nahi. Reflexive hai aur transitive bhi, lekin anti-symmetric nahi: (1, 2) aur (2, 1) dono R mein hain aur 1 ≠ 2.

short.q: f = {(1, a), (2, b), (3, a)} ek function hai A = {1, 2, 3} se B = {a, b, c} tak. Kya yeh function hai?
short.answer: Haan. A ke har element ka exactly ek image hai. Do elements (1 aur 3) ka image same ho sakta hai.

short.q: f = {(1, a), (2, b)} A = {1, 2, 3} se B = {a, b} tak. Kya yeh function hai?
short.answer: Nahi. Element 3 ∈ A ka koi image nahi hai. Function mein A ke har element ka image hona zaroori hai.

short.q: f: N → N, f(x) = x − 1 function hai ya nahi? Reason do.
short.answer: Nahi. f(1) = 0, aur 0 N = {1, 2, 3, ...} mein nahi hai (slides ka N yahi hai). Isliye f, N → N function nahi hai.

short.q: f(x) = x + 1 aur g(x) = x² ho to (g ∘ f)(x) aur (f ∘ g)(x) nikaalo.
f(x) = x + 3 aur g(x) = 3x − 4 ho to (g ∘ f)(2) aur (f ∘ g)(2) kitne hain?
A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(a, b) | a < b} irreflexive hai? Reason do.
short.answer: Haan. Kisi bhi a ke liye a < a sach nahi hai, isliye (a, a) ∉ R sab ke liye.

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(x, y) | x > y} anti-symmetric hai? Reason do.
short.answer: Haan. Agar (x, y) ∈ R, to x > y; (y, x) ∈ R ke liye y > x chahiye, jo nahi ho sakta. Isliye anti-symmetric.

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} par R = {(a, b) | a + b even} ke liye (i) reflexive (ii) irreflexive (iii) symmetric (iv) anti-symmetric check karo.
short.answer: (i) Reflexive: haan. (ii) Irreflexive: nahi, (1, 1) ∈ R. (iii) Symmetric: haan. (iv) Anti-symmetric: nahi, (1, 3) aur (3, 1) dono R mein hain.
Nahi. (3, 2) ∈ R aur (2, 3) ∈ R, lekin (3, 3) ∉ R.

short.q: A = {1, ..., 6} par R = {(x, y) | x + y odd} equivalence relation hai?
short.answer: Nahi. Reflexive nahi: (1, 1) ∉ R, kyunki 1 + 1 = 2 odd nahi hai.

short.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par R = {(x, y) | x + y ≤ 8} equivalence relation hai? Reason do.
short.answer: Haan. Reflexive: 2x ≤ 8 (x ≤ 4). Symmetric: x + y = y + x. Transitive: a, c ≤ 4 hone se a + c ≤ 8 hamesha.
Haan. f(1) = 3, f(3) = 7, f(5) = 11 — teenon B mein hain aur har input ka ek output hai.

short.q: f(x) = x² se A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} ko B = {1, ..., 25} tak function hai? Check karo.
f(x) = x + 2 aur g(x) = 2x ho to (f ∘ g)(x) aur (g ∘ f)(x) nikaalo.
f(x) = 2x + 3, g(x) = x − 5, h(x) = (x + 2)/3 ho to (f ∘ g ∘ h)(x) nikaalo.
